title: Basic dishwasher powder
subtitle: A simple four-ingredient machine detergent
excerpt: A dry dishwasher detergent of washing soda, citric acid, salt, and bicarbonate of soda. Suitable for everyday loads in soft-to-medium water. Makes about 500 g, enough for 25 washes.
sourceNotes: Washing soda and citric acid cleaning chemistry: open-access references on carbonate-based detergent formulation, EPA Safer Choice programme ingredient safety summaries (epa.gov/saferchoice). Performance limitations in hard water: UK Drinking Water Inspectorate water hardness map and manufacturer guidance on washing soda use.

recipe.yieldDescription: ~500 g powder (roughly 25 standard dishwasher loads at 20 g per load)
recipe.batchNotes: Doubles or trebles easily. Keep in a sealed, labelled container.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Make in batches of 500 g to 1 kg; the powder is stable for months.
recipe.shelfLifeNotes: Keeps one year in a sealed container in a dry cupboard. If the powder clumps, it has absorbed moisture; break up the clumps before use. Discard if it smells mouldy or fails to dissolve in the machine.

glossaryTerms.definition: Sodium carbonate crystals. A strongly alkaline salt that cuts grease and softens water. Much more alkaline than bicarbonate of soda; the two are not interchangeable.

content.text: This is a simple dry dishwasher powder built from

, citric acid, bicarbonate of soda, and table salt. The washing soda does the degreasing; the citric acid descales and rinses clean; the bicarbonate softens the water and reduces odour; the salt acts as a mild abrasive in the wash action. Works well in soft-to-medium water. In very hard water areas, increase the citric acid by 50% or add a proprietary rinse aid.

items.prepNote: 50% of powder; the main cleaning agent
20% of powder; descales and helps the glasses rinse clear

content.text: Combine in a dry mixing bowl and stir well to distribute the citric acid evenly through the washing soda base. Any unmixed pockets of citric acid will fizz on contact with the wet washing soda in the machine.
Spoon into a sealed glass jar or airtight container. Label with the dosage.
Use 20 g (about 2 tablespoons) per standard load in the main wash compartment. For heavily soiled loads, increase to 25 g.

This formula does not contain a surfactant or enzyme component, so it works less well on baked-on protein (cheese, egg, meat residue) than commercial detergents. Pre-soak heavily soiled items in hot water before loading. It also lacks a rinse-aid component; if glasses come out cloudy, add a small amount of white vinegar to the rinse-aid compartment.

Keep in a sealed container in a dry cupboard. One year shelf life. If the powder clumps solidly, it has absorbed moisture from the air; break up the clumps with a spoon before use. Store the container away from the dishwasher itself, which generates steam.
